chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
When the soul reaches this [point of no return], and he dropped his hand to his throat, there would be no repentance for the knower, and for the ignorant there would still be repentance.

key_terms.النَّفْسُ: The soul, here referring to the soul rising to the throat at death
key_terms.حَلْقِهِ: His throat, the point where the soul is drawn up
key_terms.لِلْجَاهِلِ: For the ignorant (one lacking deep knowledge/awareness)
key_terms.لِلْعَالِمِ: For the knower (one with deep knowledge/awareness)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in repentance between the knower and the ignorant at the moment of death?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (as) establishes a critical distinction in the finality of repentance (mawt al-gharam) based on spiritual awareness: the 'knower' (al-'alim) whose soul ascends to the throat loses the capacity for acceptance, while the 'ignorant' (al-jahil) retains it. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that deep, conscious knowledge of God creates a heavier accountability, where the physical signs of death preclude the spiritual state required for true repentance.
